title: Emergency Funds Explained
shortDescription: What an emergency fund is, why it matters, and the common ways people think about its size.

paragraphs: An emergency fund is money set aside specifically for unexpected, necessary expenses: a medical bill, an urgent home or car repair, or a sudden drop in income. It is not meant for planned purchases or holidays. Its job is to absorb shocks so that one bad week does not turn into months of financial strain.

bodySections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Without a cushion, an unexpected cost often has to be covered by borrowing, whether through credit, a loan, or asking family. Borrowing under pressure can be expensive and stressful, and repayments then reduce the money available in the following months. An emergency fund breaks that cycle by providing money that is already available when it is needed.
There is also a psychological benefit. Knowing that a reserve exists tends to make everyday decisions calmer, because a single surprise no longer threatens the whole month's plan.

bodySections.heading: How big is big enough?
paragraphs: A frequently cited rule of thumb is to hold enough to cover three to six months of essential expenses. Essential here means needs such as housing, food, utilities, and transport, not the full lifestyle budget.

For illustration, if essential monthly costs come to EGP 12,000, three months would be EGP 36,000 and six months would be EGP 72,000. Those figures can look daunting, which is why many people treat the full target as a long-term destination rather than a starting requirement.

The right size varies with circumstances. People with irregular income, a single earner in the household, or many dependants often aim toward the higher end of the range. Those with very stable income and few obligations sometimes consider the lower end sufficient. These are general observations, not a formula.

bodySections.heading: Building it gradually
paragraphs: A common approach is to start with a small first milestone, such as one month of essential expenses or even a round figure like EGP 5,000, and build from there. Reaching an early milestone provides immediate protection against minor emergencies and makes the larger target feel achievable.
Regular, modest contributions tend to work better than waiting for a large lump sum. Unexpected income, such as a bonus or a gift, is another opportunity some people use to speed up progress.

bodySections.heading: Where the money is kept
paragraphs: Because the purpose of an emergency fund is availability, people usually value two qualities above others: easy access when needed and stability of value. Money that could drop sharply in value, or that takes a long time to withdraw, does not serve this purpose well.
Many people also find it helpful to keep emergency money separate from everyday spending money. When the two are mixed, the fund can slowly disappear into ordinary purchases without anyone noticing.

bodySections.heading: Using and refilling it
paragraphs: Using the fund for a genuine emergency is exactly what it is for, and doing so is a sign that the plan worked. Afterwards, the common practice is to direct savings back toward the fund until it returns to its target. Over time, the emergency fund becomes the stable base on which other savings goals can be built with more confidence.
